arxiv-2011-13035.title: Star Formation in Splash Bridges Journal: ApJ
arxiv-2011-13035.creator: Travis Yeager, Curtis Struck
arxiv-2011-13035.description: Abstract Splash bridges are created from the direct collision of two gas-rich disk galaxies. These direct collisions can eject gas masses on the order of ​ 10 10 M ⊙ {10}^{10}\text{\,}\textit{M}\textsubscript{$\odot$} stripped from the stellar disks of each galaxy. The Taffy Galaxy system (UGC 1294/5) is a prototypical example of a splash bridge system.

arxiv-2012-14468.title: Fields interpretable in the free group
arxiv-2012-14468.creator: Rizos Sklinos
arxiv-2012-14468.description: Abstract We prove that no infinite field is interpretable in the first-order theory of nonabelian free groups. We also obtain a characterization of Abelian groups interpretable in this theory. 1 Introduction Tarski in 1946 asked whether the first-order theory of nonabelian free groups is complete.

arxiv-2104-09930.title: Time-quantitative density of non-integrable systems
arxiv-2104-09930.creator: J. Beck, W.W.L. Chen
arxiv-2104-09930.description: Abstract . We introduce a new method to establish time-quantitative density in flat dynamical systems. First we give a shorter and different proof of our earlier result in [ 1 ] that a half-infinite geodesic on an arbitrary finite polysquare surface 𝒫 \mathcal{P} is superdense on 𝒫 \mathcal{P} if the slope of the geodesic is a badly approximable number.

arxiv-2210-02777.title: A dynamical analogue of Ding-Iohara quantum algebras
arxiv-2210-02777.creator: Masamune Hattori, Shintarou Yanagida
arxiv-2210-02777.description: Abstract . We introduce a family of dynamical Hopf algebroids U q , p ​ ( g , X l ) U_{q,p}(g,X_{l}) depending on a complex parameter q q , a formal parameter p p , a set g g of structure functions satisfying the so-called Ding-Iohara condition, and a finite root system of type X l X_{l} .

arxiv-2410-23576.title: On the initial spin periods of magnetars born in weak supernova explosions and their gravitational wave radiation
arxiv-2410-23576.creator: Yu-Long Yan addr1, Quan Cheng e,addr1, Xiao-Ping Zheng addr1, Xia-Xia Ouyang addr1
arxiv-2410-23576.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Yu-Long Yan addr1, Quan Cheng e,addr1, Xiao-Ping Zheng addr1, Xia-Xia Ouyang addr1. The initial spin periods of newborn magnetars are strongly associated with the origin of their strong magnetic fields, both of which can affect the electromagnetic radiation and gravitational waves (GWs) emitted at their birth.

arxiv-2501-08419.title: Intermingled open and closed magnetic field lines near the radial origin of the heliospheric current sheet
arxiv-2501-08419.creator: F. S. Mozer, A. Voshchepynets, O. V. Agapitov, K.-E. Choi, L. Colomban, R. Sydora
arxiv-2501-08419.description: Abstract Purpose: To better understand the heliospheric current sheet (HCS) by describing the magnetic field geometry, the plasma, and the waves in the region near the Sun where the HCS is formed. Methods: An HCS crossing having apparent open and closed magnetic field lines was found and its fields and plasmas were analyzed.

arxiv-2510-06002.title: Deterministic Legal Agents: A Canonical Primitive API for Auditable Reasoning over Temporal Knowledge Graphs
arxiv-2510-06002.creator: Hudson de Martim
arxiv-2510-06002.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Hudson de Martim. For autonomous legal agents to operate safely in high-stakes domains, they require a foundation of absolute determinism and auditability—guarantees that standard Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) frameworks cannot provide. When interacting with temporal knowledge graphs that model the complex evolution of legal norms, agents must navigate versioning, causality, and hierarchical structures with precision, a task for which black-box vector search is ill-suited.

pmc-10537249.creator: Laura Andrade Junqueira, Francisco José Raposo, Geraldo Sérgio Farinazzo Vitral, Atabak Ghanizadeh Tabriz, Dennis Douroumis, Nádia Rezende Barbosa Raposo, Marcos Antônio Fernandes Brandão, Mattia Tiboni, Annalisa Aluigi
pmc-10537249.description: Three-dimensional printing technologies can be implemented for the fabrication of personalized vaginal rings (VRs) as an alternative approach to traditional manufacturing. This study aimed to investigate the perception of women and gynecologists regarding VRs with personalized shapes.

pmc-10754510.description: BackgroundDiffuse large B-cell lymphoma (DLBCL) is the most common B-cell lymphoma in adults. CDGSH iron sulfur domain 2 (CISD2) is an iron–sulfur protein and plays a critical role of cell proliferation. The aberrant expression of CISD2 is associated with the progression of multiple cancers. However, its role in DLBCL remains unclear.

pmc-13117639.title: DA-CycleGAN: Degradation-Adaptive Unpaired Super-Resolution for Historical Image Restoration
pmc-13117639.creator: Lujun Zhai, Yonghui Wang, Yu Zhou, Suxia Cui
pmc-13117639.description: Historical images as the dominant method for documenting the world and its inhabitants can help us to better understand the real history. Due to the limited camera technology, historical images captured in the early to mid-20th century tend to be very blurry, unclear, noisy, and obscure. The goal of this paper is to super-resolve images for historical image restoration.

pmc-13277423.title: LPLAT7 reutilizes unsaturated 1-lysophospholipids formed during lysosomal phospholipid degradation
pmc-13277423.creator: Yang Xu, Sujith Rajan, Colin K.L. Phoon, Mindong Ren, M. Mahmood Hussain, Michael Schlame
pmc-13277423.description: AbstarctLysosomal phospholipid degradation produces two types of metabolites, either 2-lysophospholipids with saturated fatty acids in sn-1 position or 1-lysophospholipids with unsaturated fatty acids in sn-2 position. They may either be degraded further or reused for phospholipid synthesis. We found that LPLAT7 (LPGAT1), an acyltransferase of the endoplasmic reticulum, reacylates specifically lysosome-derived 1-lysophospholipids that carry an unsaturated chain.

pmc-13294990.title: Targeted RNA Therapy Reprograms Fibrotic Macrophages to Reverse Pulmonary Fibrosis

pmc-13294990.description: RationalePulmonary fibrosis is driven by maladaptive immune programs that reinforce fibroblast activation.
